title: News-family Clanks: a live editorial intake/review surface must be reachable directly or via one obvious action
requirement: For a news-family Clank whose primary operator task is live editorial triage, the default operational landing surface MUST expose the live intake/review queue directly, or reach it with one obvious action (a single clearly-primary link/button, not a search through navigation).
rationale: Independently present in all three surveyed news-family Clanks, and in each case it is specifically the default/landing view, not merely present somewhere: chinese-tech-wire's Newsroom is served at both '/' and '/newsroom' (the same handler); korean-tech-wire's single page opens with 'Latest Leads' as its first section; semiconductor-intelligence's default-active tab (of 12) is explicitly 'stories'/'Editorial Inbox'. This adds something Pass 1's QC-queue standards did not establish: not just that a queue exists, but that it is the thing an operator sees first.
forbidden: A news-family Clank whose default landing view is a stats page, a source-health page, or anything else, with the live intake/review queue reachable only via a multi-step navigation search
acceptance: The default operational landing surface is, or contains, the current actionable leads/stories awaiting review
Or: the landing surface has one single, clearly-primary link/button to it — not a generic nav item indistinguishable from others
Satisfied by a dedicated route being the default, a single-page app placing it as the first/primary section, or a landing page with one obvious call-to-action into it

evidence.summary: '/' and '/newsroom' map to the same handler — the lead review queue is the default landing view.
'Latest Leads' is the first section of the single page served at '/'.
The 'stories' ('Editorial Inbox') tab is explicitly the default-active tab among 12.

notes: RATIFIED 2026-08-30 by Operator Ratification Decision 002 (decisions/0004-operator-ratification-decision-002.md). Version 2: softened from 'MUST be the default view' to the semantic requirement (direct exposure or one obvious action), so this doesn't force a literal permanent homepage-is-the-queue design — it protects CTW's, korean-tech-wire's, and semiconductor-intelligence's actual behavior without over-constraining future navigation choices. 3/3 of surveyed news-family Clanks independently satisfy this, which is the full news-family sample from this pass.
